{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01VoQDpbUEN4VtXZbu7tMyPm","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# CloudCraft, LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: http://www.naiacorp.com (SSL misconfigured; actual domain appears to be naiacorp.net)\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→CloudCraft, LLC is a product of NAIA Corporation, a small IT services and consulting firm founded in 1997 by Terry Lee in Birmingham, Alabama. NAIA originally focused on manufacturing/distribution ERP software (\"iERP\") and IT consulting for small-to-midsize businesses. The company has offices in Birmingham AL, Birmingham UK, and Dubai, with a development center in Hyderabad, India. ZoomInfo estimates 11–50 employees and under $5M in revenue. At some point NAIA expanded into healthcare IT, building \"CloudCraft Software\" as a cloud-hosted EHR platform. The CloudCraft product is branded separately from NAIA's other business lines and has its own website (cloudcraftsoftware.com), though all infrastructure runs on naiacorp.net domains and contact emails point to naiacorp.com/naiacorp.net.\n     9→\n    10→CloudCraft appears to be a very small EHR vendor. It does not appear on industry lists of top healthcare software companies in Alabama, has no reviews on G2, Capterra, or Software Advice (the Capterra listing for \"Cloudcraft\" is a completely different product — an AWS diagramming tool by Datadog), and has essentially no press coverage. The only confirmed customer visible through research is Goshen Medical Center, a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) with 38 service locations in eastern North Carolina, which uses CloudCraft's EHR and patient portal.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: CloudCraft Software\n    13→\n    14→CHPL ID: 11150 (15.04.04.3071.Clou.09.01.1.221227)\n    15→Version: 9.0\n    16→Certified: 2022-12-27\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→CloudCraft Software is described on its website as \"your all-in-one solution for electronic health records, practice management, billing, and human resources.\" It is a cloud-hosted, web-based EHR system accessible via Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox. The certified module appears to be the full product — there is no indication that CloudCraft Software is a component of a larger suite.\n    21→\n    22→The product has a broad ONC certification covering 36 criteria, including:\n    23→- **Clinical data**: (a)(1) CPOE, (a)(2) CPOE lab, (a)(3) CPOE diagnostic imaging, (a)(4) drug-drug/drug-allergy interaction checks, (a)(5) demographics, (a)(9) clinical decision support, (a)(12) family health history, (a)(14) implantable device list\n    24→- **Transitions of care**: (b)(1) transitions of care, (b)(2) clinical information reconciliation\n    25→- **Patient access**: (e)(3) patient health information capture — but notably **not** (e)(1) view/download/transmit, suggesting the patient portal may not be part of the certified module\n    26→- **Clinical quality measures**: (c)(1)–(c)(4)\n    27→- **Public health**: (f)(1) immunization registry, (f)(5) electronic case reporting, (f)(7) syndromic surveillance\n    28→- **FHIR API**: (g)(7) application access — patient selection, (g)(9) application access — all data request, (g)(10) standardized API\n    29→- **Direct messaging**: (h)(1) direct project\n    30→- **EHI export**: (b)(10)\n    31→\n    32→This is a comprehensive ambulatory EHR certification. The intended users per CHPL are \"Users at a healthcare office or facility.\"\n    33→\n    34→### Users & Market\n    35→\n    36→CloudCraft appears to target small-to-midsize ambulatory practices and community health centers. The only confirmed deployment found is **Goshen Medical Center**, an FQHC in eastern North Carolina with 38 service locations. Goshen Medical Center's website links directly to the naiacorp.net patient portal for patient access to records.\n    37→\n    38→The presence of a **sliding fee schedule module** (cloudcraft-slidingfee.naiacorp.net) is a strong signal that the product is designed for or commonly used by FQHCs, which are required to offer sliding fee discounts based on patient income. This aligns with the FQHC customer base.\n    39→\n    40→There is no information available about total number of customers, clinicians, or sites beyond Goshen Medical Center. The vendor's extremely small web footprint, lack of third-party reviews, and minimal marketing suggest a very small customer base.\n    41→\n    42→### Modules & Functionality\n    43→\n    44→The CloudCraft website describes the product as covering four main areas but provides almost no detail about specific modules or features. Information is pieced together from multiple sources:\n    45→\n    46→**Electronic Health Records (EHR):**\n    47→- Clinical charting and documentation (implied by broad (a) criteria certification)\n    48→- CPOE for medications, lab orders, and diagnostic imaging orders\n    49→- Drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking\n    50→- Clinical decision support\n    51→- Problem lists, medication lists, medication allergy lists (implied by (b)(2) reconciliation certification)\n    52→- Demographics recording\n    53→- Family health history\n    54→- Implantable device tracking\n    55→- C-CDA generation (USCDI v3 format, per the EHI export page)\n    56→- Document management — storage of scanned paper records, digital faxes, images (JPEG, GIF, TIF), Word documents\n    57→- Internal correspondence system (tasks, notes)\n    58→\n    59→**Practice Management:**\n    60→- Described on the homepage but no specific features are detailed\n    61→- Scheduling is not explicitly mentioned but is typical for this category\n    62→\n    63→**Billing:**\n    64→- Listed as a core module on the homepage but no specific features are described\n    65→- The sliding fee schedule module suggests income-based discount management for FQHCs\n    66→\n    67→**Human Resources:**\n    68→- Listed as a core module on the homepage but no details provided; unusual for an EHR product\n    69→\n    70→**Patient Portal:**\n    71→- A patient portal exists at ehrpatientportal.naiacorp.net (confirmed in use by Goshen Medical Center)\n    72→- Not certified under (e)(1) view/download/transmit, so unclear what portal capabilities are formally certified\n    73→- The (e)(3) certification suggests patients can submit health information into the system\n    74→\n    75→**FHIR API:**\n    76→- FHIR R4 server (version R4-6.0.87) accessible at fhirapitest.naiacorp.net\n    77→- Supports FHIR R4 DocumentReference resources for patient export\n    78→- Compatible with SMART on FHIR apps (MyLinks, Apple Health mentioned)\n    79→- Endpoints exposed for both \"CloudCraft Practice\" (base) and specific customer organizations (e.g., Goshen Medical Center)\n    80→\n    81→**Public Health Reporting:**\n    82→- Immunization registry reporting (f)(1)\n    83→- Electronic case reporting (f)(5)\n    84→- Syndromic surveillance reporting (f)(7)\n    85→\n    86→**Clinical Quality:**\n    87→- CQM reporting capabilities (c)(1)–(c)(4)\n    88→\n    89→**Direct Messaging:**\n    90→- Direct project messaging for secure health information exchange (h)(1)\n    91→\n    92→### Data & Content\n    93→\n    94→Based on what was found, CloudCraft stores and manages:\n    95→\n    96→- **Clinical records**: Patient demographics, problem lists, medication lists, medication allergy lists, family health history, implantable device information, clinical notes, clinical orders (medications, lab, imaging) — all implied by the certified criteria\n    97→- **Documents**: C-CDA documents (USCDI v3), PDFs (including scanned paper records and digital faxes), images (JPEG, GIF, TIF), Word documents — explicitly described on the EHI export page\n    98→- **Internal correspondence**: Tasks and notes — explicitly listed on the EHI export page as part of the exportable data\n    99→- **Immunization data**: Required for (f)(1) immunization registry reporting\n   100→- **Case report data**: Required for (f)(5) electronic case reporting\n   101→- **Clinical quality measure data**: Required for CQM reporting\n   102→- **Sliding fee/financial data**: The sliding fee module suggests income-related patient financial data\n   103→\n   104→**Gaps in information:**\n   105→- The website provides almost no detailed feature descriptions. The four-area description (EHR, PM, billing, HR) is the only product information on the main site.\n   106→- Billing capabilities are not described in any detail — it's unclear whether CloudCraft includes claim submission, ERA/EOB processing, charge capture, or other standard billing features, or if \"billing\" refers to simpler invoicing.\n   107→- Scheduling is never explicitly mentioned, though it would be expected in a practice management system.\n   108→- The \"human resources\" module is unusual for an EHR product and is not described at all. It's unclear what HR functionality is included (staff scheduling? credentialing? payroll?).\n   109→- Lab results management is not discussed (though CPOE for lab is certified, result handling is not explicitly described).\n   110→- E-prescribing is notably absent — no (b)(3) certification and no mention of Surescripts integration.\n   111→- No information about reporting or analytics capabilities beyond CQM reporting.\n   112→- No information about referral management, prior authorization, or other common ambulatory workflows.\n   113→\n   114→---\n   115→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.\n</system-reminder>\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"b7e48659-c679-42c2-9d8b-6e67c04434b6","uuid":"ddfbcf29-0b61-470f-9297-87637ec99af5","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/cloudcraft-llc--cloudcraft-software/product-research.md","content":"# CloudCraft, LLC — Product Research\n\nResearched: 2026-02-15\nDeveloper website: http://www.naiacorp.com (SSL misconfigured; actual domain appears to be naiacorp.net)\n\n## Overview\n\nCloudCraft, LLC is a product of NAIA Corporation, a small IT services and consulting firm founded in 1997 by Terry Lee in Birmingham, Alabama. NAIA originally focused on manufacturing/distribution ERP software (\"iERP\") and IT consulting for small-to-midsize businesses. The company has offices in Birmingham AL, Birmingham UK, and Dubai, with a development center in Hyderabad, India. ZoomInfo estimates 11–50 employees and under $5M in revenue. At some point NAIA expanded into healthcare IT, building \"CloudCraft Software\" as a cloud-hosted EHR platform. The CloudCraft product is branded separately from NAIA's other business lines and has its own website (cloudcraftsoftware.com), though all infrastructure runs on naiacorp.net domains and contact emails point to naiacorp.com/naiacorp.net.\n\nCloudCraft appears to be a very small EHR vendor. It does not appear on industry lists of top healthcare software companies in Alabama, has no reviews on G2, Capterra, or Software Advice (the Capterra listing for \"Cloudcraft\" is a completely different product — an AWS diagramming tool by Datadog), and has essentially no press coverage. The only confirmed customer visible through research is Goshen Medical Center, a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) with 38 service locations in eastern North Carolina, which uses CloudCraft's EHR and patient portal.\n\n## Product: CloudCraft Software\n\nCHPL ID: 11150 (15.04.04.3071.Clou.09.01.1.221227)\nVersion: 9.0\nCertified: 2022-12-27\n\n### What It Is\n\nCloudCraft Software is described on its website as \"your all-in-one solution for electronic health records, practice management, billing, and human resources.\" It is a cloud-hosted, web-based EHR system accessible via Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox. The certified module appears to be the full product — there is no indication that CloudCraft Software is a component of a larger suite.\n\nThe product has a broad ONC certification covering 36 criteria, including:\n- **Clinical data**: (a)(1) CPOE, (a)(2) CPOE lab, (a)(3) CPOE diagnostic imaging, (a)(4) drug-drug/drug-allergy interaction checks, (a)(5) demographics, (a)(9) clinical decision support, (a)(12) family health history, (a)(14) implantable device list\n- **Transitions of care**: (b)(1) transitions of care, (b)(2) clinical information reconciliation\n- **Patient access**: (e)(3) patient health information capture — but notably **not** (e)(1) view/download/transmit, suggesting the patient portal may not be part of the certified module\n- **Clinical quality measures**: (c)(1)–(c)(4)\n- **Public health**: (f)(1) immunization registry, (f)(5) electronic case reporting, (f)(7) syndromic surveillance\n- **FHIR API**: (g)(7) application access — patient selection, (g)(9) application access — all data request, (g)(10) standardized API\n- **Direct messaging**: (h)(1) direct project\n- **EHI export**: (b)(10)\n\nThis is a comprehensive ambulatory EHR certification. The intended users per CHPL are \"Users at a healthcare office or facility.\"\n\n### Users & Market\n\nCloudCraft appears to target small-to-midsize ambulatory practices and community health centers. The only confirmed deployment found is **Goshen Medical Center**, an FQHC in eastern North Carolina with 38 service locations. Goshen Medical Center's website links directly to the naiacorp.net patient portal for patient access to records.\n\nThe presence of a **sliding fee schedule module** (cloudcraft-slidingfee.naiacorp.net) is a strong signal that the product is designed for or commonly used by FQHCs, which are required to offer sliding fee discounts based on patient income. This aligns with the FQHC customer base.\n\nThere is no information available about total number of customers, clinicians, or sites beyond Goshen Medical Center. The vendor's extremely small web footprint, lack of third-party reviews, and minimal marketing suggest a very small customer base.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nThe CloudCraft website describes the product as covering four main areas but provides almost no detail about specific modules or features. Information is pieced together from multiple sources:\n\n**Electronic Health Records (EHR):**\n- Clinical charting and documentation (implied by broad (a) criteria certification)\n- CPOE for medications, lab orders, and diagnostic imaging orders\n- Drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking\n- Clinical decision support\n- Problem lists, medication lists, medication allergy lists (implied by (b)(2) reconciliation certification)\n- Demographics recording\n- Family health history\n- Implantable device tracking\n- C-CDA generation (USCDI v3 format, per the EHI export page)\n- Document management — storage of scanned paper records, digital faxes, images (JPEG, GIF, TIF), Word documents\n- Internal correspondence system (tasks, notes)\n\n**Practice Management:**\n- Described on the homepage but no specific features are detailed\n- Scheduling is not explicitly mentioned but is typical for this category\n\n**Billing:**\n- Listed as a core module on the homepage but no specific features are described\n- The sliding fee schedule module suggests income-based discount management for FQHCs\n\n**Human Resources:**\n- Listed as a core module on the homepage but no details provided; unusual for an EHR product\n\n**Patient Portal:**\n- A patient portal exists at ehrpatientportal.naiacorp.net (confirmed in use by Goshen Medical Center)\n- Not certified under (e)(1) view/download/transmit, so unclear what portal capabilities are formally certified\n- The (e)(3) certification suggests patients can submit health information into the system\n\n**FHIR API:**\n- FHIR R4 server (version R4-6.0.87) accessible at fhirapitest.naiacorp.net\n- Supports FHIR R4 DocumentReference resources for patient export\n- Compatible with SMART on FHIR apps (MyLinks, Apple Health mentioned)\n- Endpoints exposed for both \"CloudCraft Practice\" (base) and specific customer organizations (e.g., Goshen Medical Center)\n\n**Public Health Reporting:**\n- Immunization registry reporting (f)(1)\n- Electronic case reporting (f)(5)\n- Syndromic surveillance reporting (f)(7)\n\n**Clinical Quality:**\n- CQM reporting capabilities (c)(1)–(c)(4)\n\n**Direct Messaging:**\n- Direct project messaging for secure health information exchange (h)(1)\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on what was found, CloudCraft stores and manages:\n\n- **Clinical records**: Patient demographics, problem lists, medication lists, medication allergy lists, family health history, implantable device information, clinical notes, clinical orders (medications, lab, imaging) — all implied by the certified criteria\n- **Documents**: C-CDA documents (USCDI v3), PDFs (including scanned paper records and digital faxes), images (JPEG, GIF, TIF), Word documents — explicitly described on the EHI export page\n- **Internal correspondence**: Tasks and notes — explicitly listed on the EHI export page as part of the exportable data\n- **Immunization data**: Required for (f)(1) immunization registry reporting\n- **Case report data**: Required for (f)(5) electronic case reporting\n- **Clinical quality measure data**: Required for CQM reporting\n- **Sliding fee/financial data**: The sliding fee module suggests income-related patient financial data\n\n**Gaps in information:**\n- The website provides almost no detailed feature descriptions. The four-area description (EHR, PM, billing, HR) is the only product information on the main site.\n- Billing capabilities are not described in any detail — it's unclear whether CloudCraft includes claim submission, ERA/EOB processing, charge capture, or other standard billing features, or if \"billing\" refers to simpler invoicing.\n- Scheduling is never explicitly mentioned, though it would be expected in a practice management system.\n- The \"human resources\" module is unusual for an EHR product and is not described at all. It's unclear what HR functionality is included (staff scheduling? credentialing? payroll?).\n- Lab results management is not discussed (though CPOE for lab is certified, result handling is not explicitly described).\n- E-prescribing is notably absent — no (b)(3) certification and no mention of Surescripts integration.\n- No information about reporting or analytics capabilities beyond CQM reporting.\n- No information about referral management, prior authorization, or other common ambulatory workflows.\n\n---\n","numLines":115,"startLine":1,"totalLines":115}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01TQcv49WJ7XN1JoDMmLn2H2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012dCyricnDC8gALP5rFiGFD","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/cloudcraft-llc--cloudcraft-software/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# CloudCraft, LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://cloudcraftsoftware.com/certification/B10.html\n- CHPL IDs: 11150 (15.04.04.3071.Clou.09.01.1.221227)\n- Product: CloudCraft Software v9.0\n- Certified: 2022-12-27\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe** — HTTP HEAD request to the registered URL:\n   ```\n   curl -sI -L \"https://cloudcraftsoftware.com/certification/B10.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n   Result: HTTP 200, `Content-Type: text/html`, 6525 bytes. Served via CloudFront/S3. No redirects. Last-Modified: 2023-12-14.\n\n2. **Fetched the page** and examined the HTML source directly. The page is a static HTML file with no JavaScript navigation or SPA behavior. It includes a \"Download as PDF\" button implemented via `html2pdf.js` (client-side PDF generation from the rendered HTML — not a separate PDF artifact on the server).\n\n3. **Downloaded all referenced assets**: The page references 5 workflow diagram images (`img1.gif` through `img5.gif`), an arrow graphic (`arrow1.png`), the CloudCraft logo (`CloudCraft.png`), a favicon, and a CSS stylesheet. All were downloaded from `cloudcraftsoftware.com/Images/` and `/Css/styles.css`.\n\n4. **Searched for additional documentation**: Checked for downloadable files (PDF, ZIP, CSV, JSON, etc.) linked from the page — found none. The B10.html page contains no outbound links to other documentation.\n\n5. **Explored the certification site** at `cloudcraftsoftware.com/certification/`:\n   - The certification index is a separate SPA-style site with navigation links to: Home, Listing Information, Certification Criteria, Clinical Quality Measures, Safety Enhanced Design, G1/G2 Measures, Compliance Activities, Real World Testing, Case Studies.\n   - None of these navigation items link to the B10.html page — it is only accessible via its direct URL (as registered on CHPL).\n   - Checked `certificationcriteria.html`, `feature.html`, and others — all render the same generic \"Welcome to CloudCraft\" landing page with no criteria-specific content. These are placeholder pages.\n   - The mandatory disclosures URL (`cloudcraftsoftware.com/certificationdisclosurestatements`) also returns the generic landing page.\n\n6. **Probed for variant URLs**: Tested `b10.html`, `ehi.html`, `EHI.html`, `export.html`, `bulk-data.html` — all return the generic 30KB landing page. Only `B10.html` (capital B, exact match) serves the 6.5KB EHI export documentation.\n\n7. **Checked FHIR endpoint**: Attempted to reach `fhirapitest.naiacorp.net/metadata` (referenced in product research) — connection timed out. This endpoint is not publicly accessible without authentication or network access.\n\n8. **Rendered the page in a browser** and took a full-page screenshot to capture the visual workflow diagram.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe B10.html page is a single, self-contained HTML page that constitutes the entirety of CloudCraft's EHI export documentation. It is divided into two sections:\n\n### Provider Export\n\nDescribes a \"secure, one-time bulk export of all primary care provider patient data.\" The workflow is illustrated with 5 icons:\n1. Patient(s) submit requests\n2. Access Bulk Download from Admin Console\n3. Select patients requesting primary care provider access\n4. User selects secure download location\n5. User gives provider secure access\n\nThe \"Bulk Data\" section lists what the export includes:\n- C-CDA USCDI v3\n- PDF documents, including scanned paper and digital records of faxes\n- Image files (JPEG, GIF, TIF)\n- Word documents\n- Internal correspondence such as tasks, notes\n\n### Patient Export Requests\n\nDescribes a FHIR-based export pathway: \"CloudCraft FHIR supports the FHIR R4 DocumentReference resource. This resource can be used with any document format with a recognized mime type.\" Lists the same bulk data types as above, and mentions FHIR App Connections via \"MyLinks, Apple Health, etc.\"\n\n### Key Observations\n\n- The page has a typo: \"including meme document types\" (should be \"MIME document types\")\n- There is **no data dictionary** — no table definitions, no field listings, no schema\n- There is **no export format specification** beyond \"C-CDA USCDI v3\" and file types\n- There are **no sample data files or examples**\n- There are **no schema files** (no XSD, JSON Schema, OpenAPI spec)\n- There are **no API endpoint specifications** — the FHIR section mentions DocumentReference but gives no URLs, authentication details, or parameters\n- The \"Download as PDF\" button generates a client-side PDF from the HTML via html2pdf.js — there is no separate PDF artifact to download\n- The documentation has not been updated since December 2023 (per Last-Modified header)\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe documentation describes an export that includes:\n- **C-CDA USCDI v3 documents** — this covers the standard clinical data subset: demographics, problems, medications, allergies, lab results, vitals, immunizations, procedures, clinical notes, care plans, goals, and implantable devices\n- **PDF/image/Word documents** — scanned paper records, faxes, and other document attachments\n- **Internal correspondence** — tasks and notes\n\nBased on the product research, CloudCraft stores data in these domains. Assessment of coverage:\n\n| Domain | Covered? | Notes |\n|--------|----------|-------|\n| Demographics | Likely (via C-CDA) | USCDI v3 includes demographics |\n| Problems/diagnoses | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Medications | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Allergies | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Lab results | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Vitals | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Immunizations | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Procedures | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Clinical notes | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Care plans/goals | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Implantable devices | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Family health history | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Scanned documents/images | **Yes** | Explicitly listed (PDF, JPEG, GIF, TIF) |\n| Word documents | **Yes** | Explicitly listed |\n| Internal correspondence | **Yes** | Tasks and notes explicitly listed |\n| **Billing data** | **Not mentioned** | CloudCraft advertises billing as a core module; no mention of billing data in the export |\n| **Practice management data** | **Not mentioned** | No mention of scheduling, encounters, or PM data |\n| **Sliding fee/financial data** | **Not mentioned** | FQHC-specific financial data not addressed |\n| **Referrals** | **Unknown** | Not mentioned in export docs |\n| **Clinical quality measure data** | **Unknown** | Not mentioned in export docs |\n| **Order details beyond C-CDA** | **Unknown** | CPOE data structure not documented |\n\n**Critical gap: billing data.** CloudCraft advertises \"billing\" as one of its four core modules (EHR, practice management, billing, HR). Billing records are squarely within the designated record set, yet the export documentation makes no mention of billing data whatsoever. The C-CDA USCDI v3 format does not comprehensively capture billing information (charges, claims, payments, adjustments, EOBs).\n\n**The C-CDA limitation.** By describing the clinical data export as \"C-CDA USCDI v3,\" the documentation implicitly limits the structured clinical export to what C-CDA can represent. This is essentially the (g)(10) data subset. While the inclusion of documents and internal correspondence goes beyond pure (g)(10), the structured clinical data appears to be only the USCDI slice — not a comprehensive dump of everything in the database.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Primary clinical format**: C-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) conforming to USCDI v3. This is a well-established standard, but it represents the patient summary/transitions-of-care data subset, not a comprehensive database export.\n- **Document formats**: Raw files in their original formats (PDF, JPEG, GIF, TIF, DOC/DOCX). This is appropriate for document-type data.\n- **Patient-facing pathway**: FHIR R4 DocumentReference resource — documents can be retrieved via FHIR API with appropriate MIME types.\n- **No proprietary database dump**: There is no indication of a CSV, SQL, or proprietary format export that would capture all data tables. The export appears to be a curated document package, not a comprehensive data extraction.\n\nA third party receiving this export would get a C-CDA document (providing a structured clinical summary) plus attached files. This is more of a \"patient record transfer\" package than a comprehensive EHI export. The absence of a data dictionary or schema means the recipient must rely entirely on C-CDA and FHIR standards documentation to interpret the structured data.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Very poor.** The entire EHI export documentation is a single HTML page with approximately 150 words of prose content. Specific deficiencies:\n\n- **No data dictionary**: Zero field-level documentation. No table definitions, no column listings, no data type specifications.\n- **No schema files**: No XSD, JSON Schema, or any machine-readable format definition.\n- **No API documentation**: The FHIR section mentions DocumentReference but provides no endpoint URLs, authentication requirements, query parameters, or response examples.\n- **No sample data**: No example C-CDA documents, no example export packages, no sample files.\n- **No user guide**: The 5-icon workflow provides only the highest-level overview. There are no step-by-step instructions, no screenshots of the actual admin console, no explanation of options or settings.\n- **No versioning or change history**: The page appears to have been created in late 2023 and not updated since.\n- **Vague language**: \"meme document types\" (typo for MIME), \"one-time bulk export\" (is it truly one-time? can it be repeated?), \"secure Download location\" (what does this mean technically?).\n\nA developer attempting to import data from this export would need to rely entirely on knowledge of C-CDA and FHIR standards. The documentation tells you almost nothing about what specific data CloudCraft puts into the C-CDA or how their export is structured beyond the broadest categories.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Category-level only. Five bullet points listing data types. No table-level, entity-level, or field-level detail whatsoever.\n- **Coded fields**: Not documented. No value sets, no code systems, no terminology bindings.\n- **Relationships**: Not documented.\n- **Cardinality**: Not documented.\n- **Versioning**: None apparent.\n\nThis is among the most minimal EHI export documentation possible — essentially a statement that \"we export C-CDA documents plus some files.\" It meets the bare minimum of having a publicly accessible page at the registered URL, but provides almost no actionable technical detail about the export content, structure, or process.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://cloudcraftsoftware.com/certification/B10.html\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML, though browser needed to view workflow images)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The FHIR endpoint at `fhirapitest.naiacorp.net` timed out and appears inaccessible from the public internet.\n- All other URLs on the certification site (`certificationcriteria.html`, `feature.html`, etc.) serve the same generic landing page with no criteria-specific content — these are essentially placeholder pages.\n- The mandatory disclosures URL (`cloudcraftsoftware.com/certificationdisclosurestatements`) also serves the generic landing page.\n- No downloadable PDF, ZIP, CSV, or other artifact files were found anywhere on the site.\n- The \"Download as PDF\" button on B10.html generates a client-side PDF via JavaScript (html2pdf.js), not a server-hosted file.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":952,"cache_read_input_tokens":55707,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":952},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"b7e48659-c679-42c2-9d8b-6e67c04434b6","uuid":"2f5ada4e-54dd-491b-943d-0b9c627efe9d"}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012dCyricnDC8gALP5rFiGFD","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/cloudcraft-llc--cloudcraft-software/ehi-export-report.md"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"b7e48659-c679-42c2-9d8b-6e67c04434b6","uuid":"7845b84c-22bb-4e94-aef4-85b6c24189e1","tool_use_result":{"type":"create","filePath":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/cloudcraft-llc--cloudcraft-software/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# CloudCraft, LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://cloudcraftsoftware.com/certification/B10.html\n- CHPL IDs: 11150 (15.04.04.3071.Clou.09.01.1.221227)\n- Product: CloudCraft Software v9.0\n- Certified: 2022-12-27\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe** — HTTP HEAD request to the registered URL:\n   ```\n   curl -sI -L \"https://cloudcraftsoftware.com/certification/B10.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n   Result: HTTP 200, `Content-Type: text/html`, 6525 bytes. Served via CloudFront/S3. No redirects. Last-Modified: 2023-12-14.\n\n2. **Fetched the page** and examined the HTML source directly. The page is a static HTML file with no JavaScript navigation or SPA behavior. It includes a \"Download as PDF\" button implemented via `html2pdf.js` (client-side PDF generation from the rendered HTML — not a separate PDF artifact on the server).\n\n3. **Downloaded all referenced assets**: The page references 5 workflow diagram images (`img1.gif` through `img5.gif`), an arrow graphic (`arrow1.png`), the CloudCraft logo (`CloudCraft.png`), a favicon, and a CSS stylesheet. All were downloaded from `cloudcraftsoftware.com/Images/` and `/Css/styles.css`.\n\n4. **Searched for additional documentation**: Checked for downloadable files (PDF, ZIP, CSV, JSON, etc.) linked from the page — found none. The B10.html page contains no outbound links to other documentation.\n\n5. **Explored the certification site** at `cloudcraftsoftware.com/certification/`:\n   - The certification index is a separate SPA-style site with navigation links to: Home, Listing Information, Certification Criteria, Clinical Quality Measures, Safety Enhanced Design, G1/G2 Measures, Compliance Activities, Real World Testing, Case Studies.\n   - None of these navigation items link to the B10.html page — it is only accessible via its direct URL (as registered on CHPL).\n   - Checked `certificationcriteria.html`, `feature.html`, and others — all render the same generic \"Welcome to CloudCraft\" landing page with no criteria-specific content. These are placeholder pages.\n   - The mandatory disclosures URL (`cloudcraftsoftware.com/certificationdisclosurestatements`) also returns the generic landing page.\n\n6. **Probed for variant URLs**: Tested `b10.html`, `ehi.html`, `EHI.html`, `export.html`, `bulk-data.html` — all return the generic 30KB landing page. Only `B10.html` (capital B, exact match) serves the 6.5KB EHI export documentation.\n\n7. **Checked FHIR endpoint**: Attempted to reach `fhirapitest.naiacorp.net/metadata` (referenced in product research) — connection timed out. This endpoint is not publicly accessible without authentication or network access.\n\n8. **Rendered the page in a browser** and took a full-page screenshot to capture the visual workflow diagram.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe B10.html page is a single, self-contained HTML page that constitutes the entirety of CloudCraft's EHI export documentation. It is divided into two sections:\n\n### Provider Export\n\nDescribes a \"secure, one-time bulk export of all primary care provider patient data.\" The workflow is illustrated with 5 icons:\n1. Patient(s) submit requests\n2. Access Bulk Download from Admin Console\n3. Select patients requesting primary care provider access\n4. User selects secure download location\n5. User gives provider secure access\n\nThe \"Bulk Data\" section lists what the export includes:\n- C-CDA USCDI v3\n- PDF documents, including scanned paper and digital records of faxes\n- Image files (JPEG, GIF, TIF)\n- Word documents\n- Internal correspondence such as tasks, notes\n\n### Patient Export Requests\n\nDescribes a FHIR-based export pathway: \"CloudCraft FHIR supports the FHIR R4 DocumentReference resource. This resource can be used with any document format with a recognized mime type.\" Lists the same bulk data types as above, and mentions FHIR App Connections via \"MyLinks, Apple Health, etc.\"\n\n### Key Observations\n\n- The page has a typo: \"including meme document types\" (should be \"MIME document types\")\n- There is **no data dictionary** — no table definitions, no field listings, no schema\n- There is **no export format specification** beyond \"C-CDA USCDI v3\" and file types\n- There are **no sample data files or examples**\n- There are **no schema files** (no XSD, JSON Schema, OpenAPI spec)\n- There are **no API endpoint specifications** — the FHIR section mentions DocumentReference but gives no URLs, authentication details, or parameters\n- The \"Download as PDF\" button generates a client-side PDF from the HTML via html2pdf.js — there is no separate PDF artifact to download\n- The documentation has not been updated since December 2023 (per Last-Modified header)\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe documentation describes an export that includes:\n- **C-CDA USCDI v3 documents** — this covers the standard clinical data subset: demographics, problems, medications, allergies, lab results, vitals, immunizations, procedures, clinical notes, care plans, goals, and implantable devices\n- **PDF/image/Word documents** — scanned paper records, faxes, and other document attachments\n- **Internal correspondence** — tasks and notes\n\nBased on the product research, CloudCraft stores data in these domains. Assessment of coverage:\n\n| Domain | Covered? | Notes |\n|--------|----------|-------|\n| Demographics | Likely (via C-CDA) | USCDI v3 includes demographics |\n| Problems/diagnoses | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Medications | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Allergies | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Lab results | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Vitals | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Immunizations | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Procedures | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Clinical notes | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Care plans/goals | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Implantable devices | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Family health history | Likely (via C-CDA) | Standard USCDI data class |\n| Scanned documents/images | **Yes** | Explicitly listed (PDF, JPEG, GIF, TIF) |\n| Word documents | **Yes** | Explicitly listed |\n| Internal correspondence | **Yes** | Tasks and notes explicitly listed |\n| **Billing data** | **Not mentioned** | CloudCraft advertises billing as a core module; no mention of billing data in the export |\n| **Practice management data** | **Not mentioned** | No mention of scheduling, encounters, or PM data |\n| **Sliding fee/financial data** | **Not mentioned** | FQHC-specific financial data not addressed |\n| **Referrals** | **Unknown** | Not mentioned in export docs |\n| **Clinical quality measure data** | **Unknown** | Not mentioned in export docs |\n| **Order details beyond C-CDA** | **Unknown** | CPOE data structure not documented |\n\n**Critical gap: billing data.** CloudCraft advertises \"billing\" as one of its four core modules (EHR, practice management, billing, HR). Billing records are squarely within the designated record set, yet the export documentation makes no mention of billing data whatsoever. The C-CDA USCDI v3 format does not comprehensively capture billing information (charges, claims, payments, adjustments, EOBs).\n\n**The C-CDA limitation.** By describing the clinical data export as \"C-CDA USCDI v3,\" the documentation implicitly limits the structured clinical export to what C-CDA can represent. This is essentially the (g)(10) data subset. While the inclusion of documents and internal correspondence goes beyond pure (g)(10), the structured clinical data appears to be only the USCDI slice — not a comprehensive dump of everything in the database.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Primary clinical format**: C-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) conforming to USCDI v3. This is a well-established standard, but it represents the patient summary/transitions-of-care data subset, not a comprehensive database export.\n- **Document formats**: Raw files in their original formats (PDF, JPEG, GIF, TIF, DOC/DOCX). This is appropriate for document-type data.\n- **Patient-facing pathway**: FHIR R4 DocumentReference resource — documents can be retrieved via FHIR API with appropriate MIME types.\n- **No proprietary database dump**: There is no indication of a CSV, SQL, or proprietary format export that would capture all data tables. The export appears to be a curated document package, not a comprehensive data extraction.\n\nA third party receiving this export would get a C-CDA document (providing a structured clinical summary) plus attached files. This is more of a \"patient record transfer\" package than a comprehensive EHI export. The absence of a data dictionary or schema means the recipient must rely entirely on C-CDA and FHIR standards documentation to interpret the structured data.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Very poor.** The entire EHI export documentation is a single HTML page with approximately 150 words of prose content. Specific deficiencies:\n\n- **No data dictionary**: Zero field-level documentation. No table definitions, no column listings, no data type specifications.\n- **No schema files**: No XSD, JSON Schema, or any machine-readable format definition.\n- **No API documentation**: The FHIR section mentions DocumentReference but provides no endpoint URLs, authentication requirements, query parameters, or response examples.\n- **No sample data**: No example C-CDA documents, no example export packages, no sample files.\n- **No user guide**: The 5-icon workflow provides only the highest-level overview. There are no step-by-step instructions, no screenshots of the actual admin console, no explanation of options or settings.\n- **No versioning or change history**: The page appears to have been created in late 2023 and not updated since.\n- **Vague language**: \"meme document types\" (typo for MIME), \"one-time bulk export\" (is it truly one-time? can it be repeated?), \"secure Download location\" (what does this mean technically?).\n\nA developer attempting to import data from this export would need to rely entirely on knowledge of C-CDA and FHIR standards. The documentation tells you almost nothing about what specific data CloudCraft puts into the C-CDA or how their export is structured beyond the broadest categories.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Category-level only. Five bullet points listing data types. No table-level, entity-level, or field-level detail whatsoever.\n- **Coded fields**: Not documented. No value sets, no code systems, no terminology bindings.\n- **Relationships**: Not documented.\n- **Cardinality**: Not documented.\n- **Versioning**: None apparent.\n\nThis is among the most minimal EHI export documentation possible — essentially a statement that \"we export C-CDA documents plus some files.\" It meets the bare minimum of having a publicly accessible page at the registered URL, but provides almost no actionable technical detail about the export content, structure, or process.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://cloudcraftsoftware.com/certification/B10.html\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML, though browser needed to view workflow images)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The FHIR endpoint at `fhirapitest.naiacorp.net` timed out and appears inaccessible from the public internet.\n- All other URLs on the certification site (`certificationcriteria.html`, `feature.html`, etc.) serve the same generic landing page with no criteria-specific content — these are essentially placeholder pages.\n- The mandatory disclosures URL (`cloudcraftsoftware.com/certificationdisclosurestatements`) also serves the generic landing page.\n- No downloadable PDF, ZIP, CSV, or other artifact files were found anywhere on the site.\n- The \"Download as PDF\" button on B10.html generates a client-side PDF via JavaScript (html2pdf.js), not a server-hosted file.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
